The main part was written for the composer's lover, and the composer's home of Aldeburgh inspired the setting. In its prologue, Mr. Swallow, the lone supporter of the protagonist, advises him against seeking a replacement worker via Ned Keene. Though John actually slips and falls to his death, the appearance of his sweater and an earlier bruise on his neck prompt a mob led by Mrs. Sedley to pursue, FTP, the title character of what Benjamin Britten opera about a fisherman and his dead apprentices?

After a fast section in F major, the opening theme is followed by a D minor theme set over a pedal point. This piece then returns to A minor for a rising chromatic arpeggio for the right hand, and concludes with a perfect cadence. It begins in a 3/8 time signature with the right hand playing the notes of E, E flat, and E, which may allude to the person named in its title. Also known as the Bagatelle in A minor, FTP, name this short piece for solo piano by Beethoven apocryphally named for one of his students.

Selections from it appear in the lyrics to the Doors' hit single, "Show Me the Way to the Next Whisky Bar." One character is sentenced to death by Tiger Brown despite being his best friend, although that character is suddenly pardoned on the gallows and made a baron in a deliberate parody of a happy ending. Its opening scene introduces Jonathan Peacham, who controls all the beggars of London, and another scene describes the proletarian despair of an abused tavern waitress who styles herself "Pirate Jenny" in her wild, vengeful daydreams. Its songs include "Pirate Jenny's Revenge Song" and "The Ballad of Sexual Obsession," while its plot centers around the relationship between Polly and Mack the Knife. Identify this opera written by Bertolt Brecht and set to music by Kurt Weill, an adaptation of John Gay's The Beggar's Opera.

Its first movement, the "Liturgy of Crystal," is dominated by a clarinet solo which imitates the song of a blackbird, prefiguring its later "Abyss of Birds" movement. In its sixth, climactic "Dance of Fury for the Seven Trumpets" movement, no trumpets are employed, but their sound is imitated by the cello and clarinet, representing the armies of light and darkness gathered on the plains of Armageddon. The concluding "Mingling of Rainbows" movement laments the abrupt curtailment of human history. FTP, identify this piece of chamber music composed in 1931 by Olivier Messiaen.

He wrote a work for hurdy-gurdy for the King of Naples, and his version of the Orpheus myth, L'anima del filosofo, was arranged on a sponsorship from J. P. Salomon. In addition to Lo speziale and Il mondo della luna, he composed some 1,200 works in every genre, creating the Coronation Mass and The Seven Last Words of Christ for voice. Belonging both to the Baroque and the Classical periods, he wrote pieces labeled "Hornsignal," "Maria Teresa," and "Mercury," as well as the oratorio "The Creation." Patronized by the Esterhazy court, FTP, name this Austrian composer of some 108 symphonies including the London, Surprise, and Farewell.

This painter of a mural series about religion for the Boston Public Library showed a bearded man in a straw hat leaning a canvas against a fishing rod, and another man in a long blue coat ignoring a yellow-hatted woman, in paintings of Paul Helleu and Claude Monet at work. This creator of the anti- war painting Gassed showed a woman in a white dress reading over the shoulder of another in black in The Misses Vickers, and two children with paper lanterns in a flower garden in Carnation, Lily, Lily, Rose. Name this artist who depicted a pale Virginie Gautreau in a black dress under the name Madame X.

In the opening scene of this opera, "Sull'orlo dei Tetti" is interrupted by a chiming clock. The racconto "Condotta Ell'era in Ceppi" discusses the background to the story, involving a witch who was burned for giving the evil eye to the infant Garzia. Based on a play by Antonio Gutiérrez, its libretto was finished by Leone Bardare after the death of Salvatore Cammarano, expanding the part of Ines Leonora in order to counterbalance the secondary male lead, the Count di Luna. Its highlight comes just before "Stride la Vampa," when a group of Gypsies sings about work in "Chi del gitano i giorni abbella?", better known as the Anvil Chorus. Name this Verdi opera whose title refers to Manrico, a courtly singer.

It recycles the military march originally used in its composer's drama "Homecoming from Abroad." First conceived at Oban, it includes a section describing a formation at Staffa and was composed during a period of popular favor for the Ossian poems. Introducing the composer's ideas on the symphonic poem which were further developed in his 1835 Calm Sea and Prosperous Voyage, it was originally titled "The Lonely Island" and depicts the waves on a beach, columns of basalt, and the large size of the cavern which inspired it. Name this overture, composed during Felix Mendelssohn's visit to the islands on the northwest of Scotland.

Ferruccio Busoni wrote a sonatina for piano based on this composer's final opera. Trained by composer Jacques Halévy at the Paris Conservatory, he used Alfred de Musset's poem "Namouna" for the basis of his opera Djamileh. In another of his operas, Zurga sings the duet "Au fond du temple saint" with Nadir after being elected chief of a group of fishermen in Ceylon. His most famous work would later influence the realistic verismo school of dramatic opera, and includes a "seguidilla" in which the title character seduces a young corporal, as well as the Toréador Song and Habanera. FTP, name this French composer of The Pearl Fishers best known for an opera about a Spanish gypsy, Carmen.

Pale, gently rolling hills can be seen in the background of this painting below a night sky occupied by the moon and six stars. Surrounding the title figure are several possessions, including a vase, a lute, and a walking stick. Barefoot and wearing a multicolored dress, the title figure is asleep on the ground, and is being observed by a lion. FTP, what is this 1897 painting by Henri Rousseau?

When the composer finished writing this musical work, he inscribed on the manuscript "From the heart-may it go to the heart". The composer's opus 123 in D major, it was originally intended for the installation of the Archbishop of Olmutz, but would not be completed until three years after the event. Featuring the same five major sections as Bach's version in B minor, its most famous section might be the "Credo", whose forceful conclusion, the fugue "Et Vitam Venturi", is often described as the expression of the pride of a composer who believed there was something of God in him. FTP, what is this great mass by Beethoven?

The man on the far left of this painting has his head down counting the money before him on a table. Although a window is open in the top right, the main light from the scene comes from beyond the right edge of the painting. Two men in shabby clothing are arriving from the right, one of which is identified as Christ by the almost unnoticeable halo above his head. He is seen pointing to the title figure, who points at himself questioningly. FTP, what is this famous painting by Caravaggio?

The Studio is a mature expression of the late work of this painter, who upon seeing Picasso's Les Demoiselles d'Avignon said that it appeared Picasso wanted viewers to drink gasoline. Works like The Port of La Ciotat and View from the Hotel Mistral, L'Estaque come from his period as a Fauve, but he later painted innovative canvases like Houses at L'Estaque and The Portuguese, the latter of which was revolutionary for its inclusion of stenciled letters. He is best known for combining the styles of Cezanne and his close friend and collaborator Picasso to develop a new style. FTP, who was this French developer of Cubism?

The opera opens with a prologue in which wits, romantics, and low-brows who are arguing about the best form of entertainment are chased from the stage by ten announcers, who introduce the opera. In it, the jester Truffaldino tries to make the Prince of Clubs laugh to cure his melancholy. The Prince instead laughs at a pratfall of Fata Morgana, who in revenge curses him to be unhappy until he is loved by Ninetta, which he finds in the third of the three title objects. Based on a work by Gozzi, FTP, what is this farcical opera by Sergei Prokofiev?

This composer's cycle Dances of the David-Leaguers concerns an imaginary group dedicated to opposing the musical "Philistines" of the day, with each piece signed by either Eusebius or Florestan, two imaginary characters representing the composer's alternating introversion and extroversion. These characters also appear in the cycle Carnival, which is typical of his extreme Romanticism, seen in works like Carnival Jest From Vienna, the Abegg Variations, and Scenes from Childhood. FTP, who was this German composer of the Spring and Rhenish Symphonies?

Given use of the music library of A.D. Ulibishev, he began to compose at age 15, soon writing an Overture on Russian Themes. He collected folk songs from the Volga for his Second Overture on Russian Themes, which eventually became the symphonic poem Russia. Known for a despotic nature that alienated him from his disciples, as a composer he is best-known for the symphonic poem Tamara and the piano fantasy Islamey. FTP, who was this leader of the "Russian Five"?

A man in green on the left of this painting appears to be pointing to a mysterious red figure in the background seen hoisting what appears to be a cup. The titular figure is depicted in a pose intended to allude to the Deposition of Christ, and is watched by a kneeling Indian in the left foreground, who is there to place the event in North America. A man holding a large flag is directly behind the subject, who is lying on the ground beside various weapons used in the Battle of Quebec. FTP, what is this most famous painting by Benjamin West?

The impact of Cubism on this artist can be seen in his series of paintings entitled States of Mind, while works characteristic of his movement include Dynamism of a Man's Head and Dynamism of a Soccer Player. He created the first major painting of his movement with a depiction of street workers trying to control the power of draft horses amidst the urban background of Milan entitled The City Rises, but is probably best known for a sculpture cited by some as a reworking of the Winged Victory. FTP, who was this Futurist, creator of Unique Forms of Continuity in Space?

His sacred choral works include the Liturgy of St. John Chrysostom and 1915's Vespers, but more typical are his Etudes-Tableaux for piano. He wrote tone poems like The Rock and Isle of the Dead, but is better known for his piano virtuosity, displayed in works like the "Prelude in C-sharp minor". The Fitzwilliam Book is the main source of music written for this instrument, which is characterized by the placement of the keys to one side of the soundboard rather than at the end. Probably named for the Latin for "rod", FTP, what is this member of the harpsichord family perhaps also named for its use by young girls?

In his last years this painter took up lithography in the series the Bulls of Bordeaux and foreshadowed Impressionism with his portrait of J.B. Muguiro. He was occupied for 17 years with a job producing 63 cartoons for the royal tapestry factory, but later developed his own voice, as seen in his first great series of engravings, Los Caprichos. He was summoned before the Inquisition for his Clothed Maja and Naked Maja, while his deafness led to the emphasis on the savage and macabre seen in The Disasters of War. FTP, who was this great Spanish artist known for The Third of May, 1808?

Much discussion has surrounded this Raphael painting featuring two child-like angels resting their arms on a table at the bottom. Well-known for her opposition to marriage, she bore children out of wedlock with both the stage designer Gordon Craig and the sewing machine heir Paris Singer, but soon suffered tragedy when the car her children were riding in rolled into the Seine River, drowning them. Included in this painting are an advertisement for Colman's Mustard, a sign reading "Noisy Wagner Army" indicating the artist's hatred of Wagner, and most prominently a large banner in the top left reading "Viva la Sociale". In the top right with a cane and wearing a sash is the mayor, who seems to be trying to use the title event for his own advantage. The branch of a plant is seen in the hand found at the bottom of this painting. Along the top are a series of multi-colored houses and a church, below which is a man with a scythe and an upside-down woman. On the right is a man with a green face, who is staring at the head of a white horse, in whose cheek can be seen a woman milking a cow. FTP, what is this painting by Marc Chagall?

A suite of this composer's music entitled Gaite Parisienne remains popular to this day, while his only grand opera was orchestrated and provided with recitatives after his death by Ernest Guiraud. Successes like La Perichole and The Grand Duchess of Gerolstein led Rossini to dub him "our little Mozart of the Champs-Elysees". His opera-ballet Rhine Spirits came after a stint as director of his own theater, the Bouffes-Parisiens, where he developed the light French comic opera for which he is primarily famous, despite the success of The Tales of Hoffmann. FTP, who was this composer of Orpheus in the Underworld?

Just before this death, this designer of the Villa Barbaro planned the Teatro Olimpico, featuring a permanent scenic background built in architectural perspective. Characteristic of his country houses was his use of the classic temple front for the façade, while his use of arches framed between large columns became known as his motif. In Venice he designed the San Giorgio Maggiore, but most of his work was done around his home of Vicenza, including the Chiericati Palace and the Villa Rotonda. FTP, who was this great 16th century architect probably best known as the author of The Four Books of Architecture?

Works by this composer include an Easter cantata entitled Comoedia de Christi Resurrectione and a trilogy of "music dramas" consisting of Antigonae, Oedipus the Tyrant, and Prometheus. With the gymnast Dorothee Gunther he helped found the Gunther school, and in his volumes of Schulwerk published the improvisational compositions his students created under his guidance, many performed using the set of simple percussion instruments which he invented for teaching purposes. The works Songs of Catullus and The Triumph of Aphrodite complete a trilogy started with his most famous work. FTP, who is this composer of Carmina burana?

Among the designs of this architect are the French Communist Party Headquarters, Constantine University in Algeria, and a new city for Israel's Negev Desert. Famous for his sculptured, free-flowing concrete buildings, he got his start in the firm of Lucio Costa, collaborating on the Ministry of Education and Health Building in Rio de Janiero. FTP, who was this chief architect of Brasilia?

Commissioned by Ithiel Town, a green curtain has been pulled back and secured to the column on the right, allowing the viewer to see the main scene. In the back right is the ghostly image of a pyramid, in front of which are examples of both a Greek and Roman temple. Closer to the viewer is a Gothic cathedral, while in the front right is a man surrounded by books lying atop an architectural column. FTP, what is this painting by Thomas Cole?

He joined the Arte della Seta in 1398 before working in Pistoia, and was admitted as a master to the Goldsmith's Guild in 1404, the year he helped design the buttress for the Florence Cathedral. At San Lorenzo, he created a revolutionary cubic sacris ty, and he designed the first centrally planned church of the Renaissance at Santa Maria degli Angeli. FTP, identify this architect, who lost the commission for the second bronze door at the Florence Baptistry to Ghiberti.

He composed an opera, Alfonso and Estrella, and an oratorio, Lazarus, though he is better known for shorter vocal works. A great admirer of Beethoven, he would visit the composerÕs favorite coffee house, but was too afraid to speak to him; eventuall y he would be buried as close as possible to BeethovenÕs grave. Lawrence Alloway probably coined the term in 1955, using it to refer to the work of Magda Cordell, Richard Hamilton, and Paolozzi. The second wave came later, including Peter Blake and Roger Coleman, and the final group included Peter Phillips and Da vid Hockney. FTP, name this artistic movement, which uses advertising, media, and products of contemporary life, and whose American members include Claes Oldenburg, Robert Rauschenberg, Jasper Johns, Roy Lichtenstein, and Andy Warhol.

In 1600 he became court painter to Vincenzo Gonzaga, the Duke of Mantua. After returning to Flanders, he showed the influence of Caravaggio in works like the Raising of the Cross, while his Descent from the Cross shows a less dramatic style that allo wed him to employ assistants without notice. FTP, name this painter and diplomat, the teacher of Van Dyck who was knighted by Charles I.

He served as Kapellmeister to Prince Philip of Hesse for three years, after which he spent a decade touring Europe and writing operas. Educated by his father, a violinist in the ducal palace of San Marco, he was ordained a priest in 1703, although h e left the church six years later to teach violin at a girl's school. FTP, identify this baroque composer, one of the founders of the sonata and concerto form who is best known for his masterwork, The Four Seasons.

He did amateur work such as Last Hustle to Brooklyn before entering NYUÕs film school, where he won a student Academy Award for his graduation film, JoeÕs Bed-Stuy Barbershop. In 1986, SheÕs Gotta Have It established him as a talent, and he became f amous two years later with School Daze. FTP, identify this filmmaker, best known for Jungle Fever, Get on the Bus, and Do the Right Thing.

After marrying Margaret Burr, the illegitimate daughter of the Duke of Beaufort, he left London and settled in Ipswich as a portrait painter. A founding member of the Royal Academy, he retired from it in 1784, dissatisfied with the place given to hi s The KingÕs Daughters. FTP, name this painter of Cattle Crossing a Bridge, The Harvest Wagon, Mrs. Siddons, and Blue Boy.

He composed little after 1939, living in Argentina and working on an oratorio, Atlantida, which was unfinished at his death. Influenced by his friend Debussy, he composed a guitar homage to him, and his study in France affected works like the Harpsi chord Concerto and Master Peter's Puppet Show. FTP, identify this composer of Love the Sorcerer, The Three-Cornered Hat, and Nights in the Gardens of Spain.

A student of Kaminsky in Munich, he founded the Gunther school there in 1924, at the same time he was producing editions of Monteverdi's operas. Born in 1895, he composed stage works like Triumph of Aphrodite, The Clever Girl, and Oedipus the Tyrant, though he is better known for choral music. FTP, name this German composer, who disowned all of his earlier works in 1937 after the publication of Carmina Burana.

His lesser artistic achievements include a treatise on aesthetics, The Analysis of Beauty, and paintings like Pool of Bethesda and Sigismunda. Although he was influenced by the French Rococo, he was strongly anti-French, and was arrested as a spy in 1748 for drawing the fortifications of Calais. FTP, name this English artist, who got a copyright act passed in 1735 to protect engravings like his Marriage a la Mode, Harlot's Progress, and Rake's Progress from pirating.

He worked in his fatherÕs butchery until 1857, when he was sent to organ school. Gaining fame with a cantata based on HalekÕs The Heroes of the White Mountain, he was befriended by Brahms, who helped him win the commission for the Slavonic Dances. F TP, identify this composer of the Dumky trio and Rusalka, who is best known for his ninth symphony, ÒFrom the New World.Ó

Trained as an engineer before entering the Art Student's League school in 1923, his first fame came with the miniature puppet circus he designed in France. Originally a sculptor in wood and wire, he was inspired by a meeting with Mondrian to work wi th nonobjective constructions. FTP, name this American artist, whose Little Spider, Teodelapio, and Three Arches are the best known of his stabiles and mobiles.

He hosts such segments as the Monday Ratings Report and Cooking With..., as well as singing the closing theme in his distinctive shriek. Andy Merrill, who also dresses in the Space Ghost costume, has made this character the real star of the Cartoon N etwork's Cartoon Planet. FTP, name this 1960's rival of Space Ghost, who until recently was not animated to explode.

His written works include The Fifth String and Pipetown Sandy, though he is better known as a musician. Composer of numerous comic operas, such as The Bride Elect and Chris and the Wonderful Lamp, he also wrote 15 orchestral suites, many songs, and The Chariot Race, a symphonic poem. FTP, identify this American, who organized a band in 1892, twelve years after taking over the U.S. Marine corps band, best known for marches like The Washington Post and Stars and Stripes Forever.

The son of a weaver, he decided to compose operas when he first heard Rossini at the Naples Conservatory. He wrote his first opera, Enrico di Borgogna, while serving in the army, and went on to success with 1822's Zoraide di Granata, which led to hi s exemption from military service. FTP, name this composer, who spent three years in a mental institution prior to his death at the age of 51, best known for Don Pasquale, Anna Bolena, Lucia di Lammermoor, and The Elixir of Love.

He worked as a landscape painter in Philadelphia before going to London in 1786 to study under Benjamin West. In 1794, he got a British patent for a double-inclined plane that would make locks obsolete, and he invented a mill for polishing marble. F TP, name this American inventor, who worked in Paris on a submarine torpedo boat before returning to New York, where, in 1807, he launched the Clermont, the first successful steamboat.

The son of a painter and a pianist, this man entered the conservatory in 1835 and studied under the Bohemian composer Anton Reicha. He was influenced by Palestrina and wrote many sacred and choral works, such as Mass for St. CeciliaÕs Day and the we ll known Ave Maria. Among his first projects in the public realm was the New York State Theater, but after that construction he rejected his earlier style, leading to works like the neo-gothic PPG Place in Pittsburgh, and stainless steel prisms surround the Bell Tower of his Crystal Cathedral. His collaborations with John Burgee include the Puerta de Europa in Madrid and a building in New York City which features the so-called "Chippendale" pediment. That building was originally named for AT&T, and this man is perhaps most famous for his own residence in New Canaan, Connecticut, built in collaboration with Richard Foster.
